title: Gentlemen Ransomware Affiliate Uses MCP as C2 Channel in Live Cyberattacks
key_facts: CloudSEK report dated 5 Oct 2026 on a Gentlemen ransomware affiliate calling himself Azazel
Exposed open directory and storage servers held more than two dozen victim directories and about 6TB of stolen data across six countries
The affiliate also ran his own leak site, LEAKNED, keeping proceeds from the ransomware operator
A script called MCP exec_in_session on a locally bound server to loop SSH checks across six internal hosts
CloudSEK says it found no prior public report of MCP used operationally as a C2 channel in a live criminal campaign
Beacon logs showed scanning for exposed MCP server ports under the name 'internet-census-mcp-scanner'
Mitigation advice: never bind an MCP server beyond strict loopback and audit exec_in_session
quote_evidence: CloudSEK has not identified prior public reporting of a threat actor operationally using MCP exec_in_session as a C2 channel in a live criminal campaign.
Each check was executed via exec_in_session MCP calls to 127.0.0.1:35367 this script is the confirmed operational use of MCP as an attack execution channel in this investigation.
why_it_matters_hint: Criminals reported to use an AI-tool connection standard to run attack commands.
notes: GBHackers page gave no text (HTTP 202); written from CloudSEK's own report, the first source. CloudSEK's report is dated 5 Oct 2026.
